introduction:
A Death Certificate in Karnataka is a vital legal document certifying the demise of a person, governed by the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. It is essential for settling insurance claims, property transfer, bank account closures, and other legal processes.

Registration can be initiated online via the Seva Sindhu portal or offline at local municipal/panchayat bodies, followed by downloading the digitally signed certificate from the eJanMa portal.
quickFacts:
Critical Guidelines
  • Time Limit: The death must be registered with the concerned local authorities within 21 days of its occurrence.
  • Fees: For online submissions via the Seva Sindhu portal, a service charge of ₹35 is applicable. In-person registrations at municipal or panchayat offices may also charge a small fee.
  • Eligibility: Citizens of India.
documentsRequired:
Documents Required for Death Registration

Note: Ensure you have scanned copies for online uploads and original documents for physical verification.
Proof of Death
  • Cremation Certificate / Receipt from the crematorium or burial ground.
  • Form 4 / Form 4A (Medical Certificate of Cause of Death).
  • Form 2 (Death Reporting Form).
  • Declaration document.
  • An affidavit specifying the date & time of death OR a death slip/cause sheet provided by a doctor.
Identity & Address Proofs
  • Aadhaar card of the deceased (highly recommended).
  • ID card of the applicant (Aadhaar, Voter ID, PAN).
  • Address Proof / Residential Proof of the deceased.
  • Proof of birth of the deceased (SSLC, Birth Certificate, etc.).
onlineApplication:
Online & Digital Registration Methods

Method A: Via Seva Sindhu Portal
  1. Visit the Seva Sindhu Portal.
  2. Click on the "Departments & Services" tab in the menu.
  3. In the search box, type "death" and click the search icon.
  4. Select either the "Application for Death Certificate" or "Application for Death Registration" option.
  5. Review the guidelines, required documents, and fees, then click on "Apply Online".
  6. In the login window, enter your Login ID and OTP/Password to log in.
  7. If you are a new user, click on "Register Here" and complete the registration using your Aadhaar number and DigiLocker account.
  8. Once logged in, fill out the application details, attach the necessary documents, pay the service charge of ₹35, and submit.
Method B: Via Common Service Centres (CSC) (Requires Offline Visit)
  1. Go to the official CSC locator website (locator.csccloud.in).
  2. Select your State, District, Sub-District, and CSC Pay Agent to search for the nearest CSC agents in your area.
  3. Once you get the contact information of nearby agents, visit the nearest CSC center in person with all the required documents.
  4. The operator will fill out and process the online application on your behalf. You may need to pay a small processing fee.
offlineApplication:
Method C: Offline Registration at Local Offices

Step-by-Step Process:
  1. Ensure registration within 21 days: The death should be officially reported by the appropriate person:
    - House death: The Head of the Family.
    - Hospital death: The Medical Officer in-charge.
    - Jail death: The Jailer in-charge.
    - Deserted/Public body: The Village Headman or local Police Station in-charge.
  2. Approach Local Office: Visit the local Municipality office or Panchayat office under whose jurisdiction the death occurred.
  3. Collect Application Form: Request the death registration application form from the concerned officer.
  4. Submit Details: Fill out the prescribed form and submit it along with all the supporting documents (cremation receipt, doctor's death slip, Form 2/4, ID proofs).
  5. Official Issuance: The local authorities will process the entry in their records and issue the death certificate.
afterApplying:
Certificate Issuance & Download

  • Home Delivery: In most cases, the physical death certificate will be delivered directly to your home address via post/speed post.
  • Online Download: You can download and print the certificate online. Visit the official eJanMa Portal, click on "Download Certificate", and follow the user manual instructions to download the death certificate using your application details.
